info.title: Clover CMS API
info.description:
REST API for the Clover agency platform.

**Authentication schemes:**

**AdminBearer** — JWT obtained after a two-step login:
1. `POST /api/auth/login` — validates password, emails a 6-digit OTP
2. `POST /api/auth/verify-otp` — validates OTP, returns a 7-day JWT

New admin accounts must also verify their email before they can sign in (`POST /api/auth/register` → link in email → `GET /api/auth/verify-email?token=...`).

**ClientBearer** — opaque 30-day session token issued by `POST /api/portal/verify-otp`. Stored in the database; logging out invalidates it immediately.

Pass either token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

AdminBearer.description: Admin JWT — obtained after 2-step login (`POST /api/auth/login` → `POST /api/auth/verify-otp`). Valid for 7 days. The JWT encodes the admin's role (`ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN`). Super-admin-only endpoints return 403 for regular admins.

ClientBearer.description: Client session token — obtained from `POST /api/portal/verify-otp`. Valid for 30 days. Stored in the database; logging out invalidates it immediately.

approved.description: Must be true (set by super admin) before the admin can sign in

resultingProjectId.description: Set on approval — the new project for `new_project`, or the parent project itself for `new_phase` (symmetric across both approval types)

post.summary: Approve a revision request
post.description:
Two approval modes:
- `new_project` — scaffolds a new Project linked to the original via `parentProjectId`. Requires `projectName`.
- `new_phase` — the admin authors the phase inline: creates the given `milestones` on the *existing* project (tagged with `phase`, appended after the current max order), sets `Project.phase` to `phase`, and — if `endDate` is given and later than the current one — extends `Project.endDate`. `resultingProjectId` is set to the parent project itself, symmetric with `new_project`. Requires `phase` and at least one entry in `milestones`.

Client is notified by email in both cases, including `decisionNote` if provided.

phase.description: Required when type is new_phase — phase label written to the new milestones and to Project.phase

milestones.description: Required when type is new_phase — at least one entry

endDate.description: Optional, new_phase only — extends the project's target finish. Ignored if earlier than the current endDate.

decisionNote.description: Note shown to the client alongside the approval

400.description: phase is required for new_phase approvals / At least one milestone is required for new_phase approvals

get.summary: List the calling admin's notifications, newest first
get.description: Capped at the 50 most recent. `INVOICE_OVERDUE` and `MILESTONE_DUE` are derived lazily on each call from current invoice/milestone state (there is no background scheduler); `REVISION_REQUESTED` and `DELIVERABLE_REVIEW` are created at the moment those events happen, for every approved admin. Intended to be polled roughly every 60s. There is no separate unread-count endpoint — derive it client-side from `data.filter(n => !n.read).length`.

patch.description: 404s if the notification does not belong to the calling admin.

read.description: Pass false to mark unread again

get.description: Each deliverable includes the client's own latest `review` on that version, so the portal can show "You approved this" / "Changes requested" durably instead of resetting on reload.

get.description: Collapses the per-project invoice fan-out into a single request for the dashboard billing snapshot. Excludes DRAFT invoices.

post.summary: Submit a review on a deliverable
post.description: Client approves or requests changes. Admin is notified by email. Only READY deliverables can be reviewed.

409.description: Deliverable is not in READY status

post.summary: Submit a revision request on a project
post.description: Client describes what they need. Admin is notified by email and an in-app notification, and the client gets a "received" acknowledgement email; the request enters the revision queue. Pass `deliverableId` to promote a deliverable "request changes" review into a linked revision request — this is a deliberate, opt-in action taken by the client, not automatic.

description.example: We need an additional page for our new product line.

deliverableId.description: Optional — links this request to the deliverable it was raised from. Must belong to the same project.

404.description: Project not found / Deliverable not found

get.summary: List all of the client's revision requests
